edits.name: manual-entry-example
edits.description: Manual-entry examples for monthly airline passengers, annual Nile flow volume and monthly Mauna Loa CO2, with source CSV files. The Nile project dates are 1897–1996 while the CSV dates are 1871–1970; compare and reconcile dates before historical interpretation.
edits.oldDescription: Demonstrates manual time series data entry using copy-paste from CSV files. Contains three classic datasets commonly used in time series analysis: airline passengers, Nile River annual flows, and atmospheric CO2 concentrations.

edits.name: Airline Passengers
edits.description: Monthly airline passenger totals (Box-Jenkins, 1970). A classic dataset for seasonal ARIMA modeling, exhibiting strong seasonality and multiplicative trend. Saved coverage: 1949-01-01 through 1960-12-01; 144 ordinates, 0 missing; interval setting OneMonth.
edits.oldDescription: Monthly airline passenger totals (Box-Jenkins, 1970). A classic dataset for seasonal ARIMA modeling, exhibiting strong seasonality and multiplicative trend.

edits.name: Nile River Flows
edits.description: Annual Nile flow volumes in 10^8 cubic metres. Saved dates are 1897–1996; the supplied CSV dates are 1871–1970. Values and dates are retained for a documented date-reconciliation exercise. Saved coverage: 1897-01-01 through 1996-01-01; 100 ordinates, 0 missing; interval setting OneYear.
edits.oldDescription: Annual flow volume of the Nile River at Aswan (Cobb, 1978). A classic dataset for change-point detection and AR modeling, with a notable level shift around 1898.

edits.name: Mauna Loa CO2
edits.description: Monthly atmospheric CO2 concentrations from Mauna Loa Observatory, Hawaii (NOAA GML). A classic dataset for seasonal decomposition with strong upward trend and annual cycle. Saved coverage: 1958-03-01 through 2023-12-01; 790 ordinates, 0 missing; interval setting OneMonth.
edits.oldDescription: Monthly atmospheric CO2 concentrations from Mauna Loa Observatory, Hawaii (NOAA GML). A classic dataset for seasonal decomposition with strong upward trend and annual cycle.

edits.name: USGS - 11274500 - Peaks-Over-Threshold
edits.description: USGS - 11274500 - Peaks-Over-Threshold: 78 saved observations indexed 1937–2025, with 0 low-outlier flags. POT teaching example for Orestimba Creek daily mean discharge, USGS 11274500. Saved threshold 650 cfs, separation 5 daily steps, no smoothing, 78 events. Older input lacks source-exposure metadata and uses 89 retained-event years (Lambda 0.8764044944), although the daily source spans 1932–2026. Resolve exposure before annual-frequency use.
edits.oldDescription: Peaks-Over-Threshold (POT) series extracted from daily discharge at USGS gage 11274500 (Orestimba Creek near Newman, CA). Uses a threshold of 650 cfs with a minimum separation of 5 days between peaks, yielding 78 independent flood events over 94 years of record (~0.8 events/year). Threshold diagnostics (MRL plot, modified scale and shape stability plots) support the selected threshold.
